why: The one review of the leakgrep-patch-blob-quotes slice at 5d1e0ba62, today's lead tooling: sent back to tests with one blocking class. The fix in leakgrep.sh is right: in --commits mode a patch line is quoted only when the commit's own blob has that line inside a hunk at that new-file number. A scratch probe showed it holds for a merge (per parent), a root commit, a rename inside patches/, a rename out of it, CRLF, a missing final newline, and a path with a space or a non-ASCII name (both flag, fail closed). The gap is in the laws: no law adds an outer line whose text also stands inside a hunk but at a number outside every hunk. A scratch copy that looks the text up anywhere in the quoted lines, ignoring the number, keeps all 39 laws of leakgrep.patches.test.ts green, and lets an em dash added before the patch's first @@ pass when the same text sits in a hunk.
note: The five leakgrep test files ran 97 passed of 97 at 5d1e0ba62. loosening.sh from the merge base 2623b9f39 printed two hits, both new or changed code (leakgrep.patches.test.ts line 281, leakgrep.sh line 32), no law loosened; run against origin/main it printed several hundred hits that are main's own later commits, since main moved to c8d2646d0. leakgrep --commits on the branch range printed 3 commits read, added text clean. git merge-tree with origin/main shows no conflict. The plant ran on a scratch copy through TEST_LEAKGREP; no branch file was touched.
